summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem has become the de facto standard for connecting AI agents to external tools, data sources, and services through a unified interface. By 2026, adoption spans three layers: aggregator platforms that bundle thousands of integrations behind one endpoint, gateways that handle routing/auth/observability, and individual servers that expose specific capabilities like browser automation or repository access. This matters because MCP eliminates bespoke integration work, letting agents securely discover and invoke tools at scale.
ecosystem_note: Aggregators expose many services through a single managed endpoint, gateways sit in front of servers to handle routing, auth, and observability, while individual servers each connect an agent to one specific tool or capability.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.connects_to: Browser automation — navigating pages, clicking, filling forms, scraping, and running end-to-end web tasks via a controlled browser
strengths: Most-used individual MCP server in the community per public usage rankings
Backed by Microsoft and the mature Playwright project
Reliable cross-browser automation without screenshots-only hacks
tools.best_for: Agents that need to drive real browsers for testing, scraping, or web task automation

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.connects_to: GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, actions, and code search with OAuth-secured remote access
tools.pricing_paid: Included with GitHub plans; free tier available
strengths: Official OAuth-secured remote MCP server
Deep coverage of repos, issues, and PR workflows
First-party vendor backing and frequent updates
tools.best_for: Automating repository management, issue triage, and code review workflows

tools.name: Context7
tools.connects_to: Up-to-date, version-specific library and framework documentation injected into agent context
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans for higher usage
strengths: Consistently cited as a top pick across IDEs and Codex 1.x
Reduces hallucinated APIs by supplying current docs
Simple setup and broad library coverage
tools.best_for: Coding agents that need accurate, current documentation for dependencies

tools.name: Composio
tools.connects_to: One endpoint for 1,500+ apps (GitHub, Slack, CRMs, databases) with managed auth, structured schemas, and dynamic tool routing
tools.pricing_paid: Usage-based paid plans for teams and production scale
strengths: 1B+ tool calls run on the platform with a self-learning tool-selection layer
Fastest onboarding for broad SaaS tool access
Managed auth across many integrations
tools.best_for: Giving an agent fast access to a large library of SaaS products through one integration

tools.name: Figma MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Figma design files, components, and design context for generating code and extracting design data
strengths: Official OAuth-secured remote server
Bridges design-to-code workflows for agents
Strong adoption among front-end and design engineers
tools.best_for: Turning Figma designs into code or extracting design specs within agent workflows

tools.name: Smithery
tools.connects_to: Registry and hosting for thousands of MCP servers with one-click discovery, deployment, and config management
tools.pricing_paid: Paid tiers for hosted and team usage
strengths: Largest MCP server registry for discovery
Simplifies installing and hosting community servers
Centralized config across clients
tools.best_for: Discovering and deploying MCP servers without manual local setup

tools.name: Supabase MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Supabase Postgres databases, auth, storage, and edge functions via OAuth-secured remote MCP
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Supabase plans; free tier available
strengths: Official remote MCP with database-native operations
Lets agents query and manage backends directly
Popular among full-stack developers
tools.best_for: Agents managing database schemas, queries, and backend operations on Supabase

tools.name: Cloudflare MCP
tools.connects_to: Hosting and routing remote MCP servers on Cloudflare Workers with OAuth, edge deployment, and observability
tools.pricing_paid: Workers paid plans for higher usage
strengths: Edge-hosted remote MCP with built-in OAuth
Eliminates local install and credential leakage risk
Strong infrastructure backing for production deployments
tools.best_for: Deploying secure, remote MCP servers at the edge for production agents

tools.name: Notion MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Notion pages, databases, and workspace content via OAuth-secured remote MCP
strengths: Official remote server with OAuth security
Enables agents to read and write knowledge-base content
Widely adopted for docs and project management automation
tools.best_for: Agents managing documentation, notes, and structured workspace data in Notion

tools.name: Stripe MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Stripe payments, customers, invoices, and billing data via OAuth-secured remote MCP
tools.pricing_paid: Free to use; standard Stripe transaction fees apply
strengths: Official remote server for payment and billing operations
Secure OAuth access to financial workflows
Trusted vendor backing for production use
tools.best_for: Agents automating payment, invoicing, and billing tasks on Stripe

tools.name: mcp.so
tools.connects_to: Public directory indexing thousands of MCP servers for search, discovery, and comparison
strengths: One of the largest community MCP directories
Fast discovery of new and trending servers
No account required to browse
tools.best_for: Browsing and comparing the full catalog of available MCP servers

tools.name: Docker MCP
tools.connects_to: Containerized MCP servers via the Docker MCP Catalog and Toolkit with sandboxed, reproducible execution
strengths: Sandboxed, reproducible server execution in containers
Curated MCP catalog with secure defaults
Integrates cleanly with existing Docker workflows
tools.best_for: Running MCP servers in isolated, reproducible containers for security and consistency
